Rounds.How opened: June 24 board decision launched broad preliminary outreach; CSC contacted by June 28.
Rounds.Who was in: 50 outreach prospects: 15 strategic (A, CSC/Pamplona, 13 others) and 35 financial (B, C, 33 others). Initial-stage access individually dated for CSC/Pamplona, B and C; 16 other financial NDA/information recipients have uncertain dates. Party A already live by its June 21 bid, but not admitted to confidential review until August 5. Twenty eventual NDA signers is not July 23 eligibility.
Rounds.Bids received: 3: CSC/Pamplona (Strategic), Party B and Party C (Financial). A’s June 21 bid is round 0 and remained under consideration; no new round 1 A bid. No other-scope bids.
Rounds.How it ended: July 25: B, C and CSC/Pamplona advanced, A conditionally admitted on an NDA. B and C missed July 23 but continued; C revised in writing July 25. Sixteen anonymous financial signers inferred excluded by August 27; precise earlier eligibility/exit timing unresolved (Q5).

Rounds.How opened: July 25 selection for management meetings, staged information and revised offers.
Rounds.Who was in: 3 admitted at opening: CSC/Pamplona (Strategic), B and C (Financial). A (Strategic) eligible conditionally, admitted August 5. Then 4 admitted, 2 Strategic + 2 Financial. At opening, 4 known live units including A, plus up to 16 anonymous financial entrants with uncertain timing; those 16 not shown admitted and inferred excluded by August 27. No continuing partial alternative.
Rounds.Bids received: 4: CSC/Pamplona, Party A, Party B and Party C. No other-scope bids.
Rounds.How it ended: All four invited to final indications September 11. A and C missed September 9 but bid September 10 and continued; C responded orally despite the written request. No rival eliminated among these four.

Rounds.How opened: September 11 calls requested final indications by September 18.
Rounds.Who was in: 4 admitted/live: CSC/Pamplona and Party A (2 Strategic); Party B and Party C (2 Financial). No other bidder carried forward. C then did not submit; A and B displaced by September 24 exclusivity. CSC/Pamplona alone through signing.
Rounds.Bids received: 3: CSC/Pamplona, Party A and Party B. Later CSC funding/liability revisions count once for bidder totals. No other-scope bids.
Rounds.How it ended: C did not submit and exits by September 18. Target selected CSC/Pamplona for $21.25 counter; September 24 exclusivity excludes A/B. Exclusivity extended October 12; signed October 14. No missed-deadline bidder continued in this round.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: is this one process with three rounds, and where do the stages start?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep one process: round 1 June 24 outreach decision (CSC contacted by June 28), round 2 July 25 staged diligence/updated offers, round 3 September 11 final solicitation. April approach and June 21 bid remain round 0.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 27–41. Sale-contact gap: April 8–June 21, 2013 (74 days). E5(a) fails: Party A retained in view; (b) fails: no termination or three-month break; (c) June outreach is fresh but insufficient alone. The 2011–2012 CSC acquisition and related adviser-only interval are not a Mac-Gray sale attempt.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Plausible alternative delays round 2 to August 27, moving July 25–August 26 stage-2 events into round 1. Reject under E6: admission/diligence and its later submission letter form one stage. No supported separate-process alternative.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how was the July 23 preliminary deadline treated?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). B and C first responded July 24; C supplied a written revision July 25. A’s earlier unsolicited offer remained under consideration, without July 23 NDA eligibility.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 32–34: July 23 due date; dated July 24 responses and July 25 review/advancement. No new bid due date set. C’s later July 25 written proposal remains an initial-stage response.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would change round 1 timing interpretation. Party A is not a July 23 non-submitter. No late responder exits or re-enters.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how was the September 9 revised-offer deadline treated?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). Accept September 10 offers from A and C within round 2, including C’s oral response to a written-proposal request.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 35–36: CSC/Pamplona and B bid September 9; A and C September 10; all four evaluated September 11 and invited to final offers. No extension date stated.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would change deadline classification; treating A/C as exits would contradict their immediate continued participation.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention/permitted inference: was the September 18 final deadline enforced, and did Party C exit?
Questions.Recommended answer: Enforced. Three final responders were assessed September 19; infer C’s participation ended at its non-response. September 21 CSC/Pamplona improvement answers a fresh target counter within the same final round.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 36–37: C neither submitted nor reiterated and gave no reason; no later C involvement. September 19 target selection and September 21 price bargaining are distinct from overdue submissions.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: An alternative late-acceptance reading changes the deadline outcome; retaining C would increase live final-round rivals until exclusivity. No evidence supports an exit valuation reason.

Questions.Question: Source gap/permitted inference: when were the 16 anonymous financial NDA signers admitted and excluded?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep 16 residual financial signers (18 less B/C), with June 24–August 24 execution window. Infer exclusion by August 27, when all NDA entries precede the complete four-party continuing solicitation. Do not subtract 20 minus four at July 23.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 32–35: 50 contacts = 15 strategic + 35 financial; 20 NDAs = A + CSC/Pamplona + B + C + 16. July 25 advancement names four, but some anonymous NDAs may be later. Individual eligibility and exclusion dates are missing.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Earlier individual NDA dates could support some July 23 Did not submit or July 25 exclusions. Delaying residual closure to exclusivity/signing raises live counts beyond August 27. Round 2 opening has four known live bidders plus up to 16 timing-uncertain residuals; four admitted by August 5.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: should Party B’s performance options be contingent consideration or upfront stock?
Questions.Recommended answer: Use $19 upfront cash, Stock %=0, CVR/earnout=Y and $2.50 bidder-stated value. Preserve $21.50 package value separately; $2.50 is not a guaranteed payout or maximum.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 36–37: options represent 10% new equity at initial-cost strike; vest on achievement of no-acquisition management projections over five years. Board explicitly discusses contingent/deferred payment and measurement risk. E13 treats performance-dependent securities as contingent payment.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Upfront-stock treatment increases reported upfront price to $21.50 and changes the cash/stock mix. No comparable stock percentage is supported if contingent options are treated separately.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention/source gap: how should final bargaining and later commitment revisions be classified?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep September 21 and September 21–23 proposals Formal as responses within the genuine final solicitation. October 5 commitment-letter markup is Formal; October 8 oral cap proposal is Informal. Record both material liability revisions, leaving their unstated prices/mixes blank.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 36–40. A expressly reiterates its previous indication September 18, permitting financing-term carryover. CSC’s later bids do not expressly carry all earlier terms. October 8 reports a telephone proposal, not a new markup. No later signed financing is backdated.

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: U.S. dollars per Mac-Gray common share. Price columns are upfront value. Party B September 18: $19 cash plus options valued by B at $2.50 per share, for its stated $21.50 package; contingent amount recorded separately (p. 36).

BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated). Earlier CSC-acquisition engagement terminated May 15; strategic-review engagement approved May 30, signed May 31 (pp. 27, 29–30).
Goodwin Procter LLP (p. 27).

Mac-Gray explored strategic alternatives and approached Party A before launching broad sale outreach in June 2013. The banker contacted 50 prospects, and 20 ultimately signed confidentiality agreements, although individual timing is incomplete. Four named bidders reached staged diligence, with less customer information initially provided to the two strategic bidders. After revised offers and a final September solicitation, Party C stopped submitting, while Party B offered cash plus performance-dependent options and Party A held at $18–19 cash. Mac-Gray negotiated CSC/Pamplona to $21.25 cash, granted exclusivity, and negotiated sponsor funding and liability commitments. The merger agreement was signed October 14 and announced October 15; no post-signing competing proposal or go-shop is reported.

Rounds.How opened: Special Committee decides to consider a sale and has BofA approach 50 parties (15 strategic, 35 financial); outreach and NDAs follow from 06/28 (#9).
Rounds.Who was in: NDA signers furnished the informational package: CSC/Pamplona (strategic); Party B, Party C (financial); and up to 16 other financial NDA signers (execution dates not given; 20 NDAs in total over about two months). Not admitted, bid still being received: Party A (strategic), whose 06/21 proposal was outstanding and whose NDA stalled until 08/05.
Rounds.Bids received: 3: CSC/Pamplona (S) $18.50; Party B (F) $17-18; Party C (F) $15-17 oral, then $16-16.50 written. Party A's round-0 06/21 proposal ($17-19) was reviewed alongside them.
Rounds.How it ended: Four advanced on 07/25 (Party A, subject to an NDA; Party B; Party C; CSC/Pamplona). The other 16 financial NDA signers are out (inferred). Party B and Party C missed 07/23 but continued, submitting on 07/24-07/25.

Rounds.How opened: Special Committee selects four bidders for management meetings and staged diligence, to be followed by revised indications (#27); the letter of 08/27 set the due date.
Rounds.Who was in: 4: strategic Party A (NDA 08/05) and CSC/Pamplona; financial Party B and Party C. Financial bidders had broad data-room access; strategic bidders had limited access without customer data, plus synergy talks.
Rounds.Bids received: 4: CSC/Pamplona (S) $19.50; Party B (F) $18.50; Party A (S) $18-19; Party C (F) $16-17 oral.
Rounds.How it ended: All four invited to the final round on 09/11. Party A and Party C missed 09/09 but continued, submitting on 09/10.

Rounds.How opened: BofA calls all four requesting final indications of interest by 09/18, with a possible short exclusivity for one bidder (#38).
Rounds.Who was in: 4: strategic Party A and CSC/Pamplona; financial Party B and Party C.
Rounds.Bids received: 3: CSC/Pamplona (S) $20.75; Party A (S) reiterated $18-19 as best and final; Party B (F) $19.00 cash plus options it valued at $2.50 ($21.50 package). Party C did not submit.
Rounds.How it ended: CSC/Pamplona selected (09/19), raised to $21.25 (09/21), and given exclusivity (09/24, extended 10/12). Party A and Party B dropped at exclusivity (inferred); Party C did not submit. Signing 10/14/2013.

Questions.Question: Process and round map (choice of convention). Is this one process with round 1 opening 06/24/2013, round 2 on 07/25 and round 3 on 09/11? Gaps of about two months or more with no reported contact with a prospective acquirer: 10/23/2012-04/08/2013, and 04/08/2013-06/21/2013 (about 2.5 months).
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep one process and three rounds. The 04/05 authorization, the 04/08 call and Party A's 06/21 proposal stay in round 0. E5 tests for a break before 06/24: (a) fails, Party A kept in view; (b) fails, gap under three months; (c) holds, 06/24 decision.
Questions.Why, with page: The 04/05 mandate was to explore 'transactional opportunities', and the Board deferred a sale process to 05/09 and 06/24 (pp. 27-31). The first organized outreach followed the 06/24 decision (p. 32). The 07/25 selection and the 09/11 final request are distinct stages (pp. 34, 36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative: treat 04/05 as the sale decision and open round 1 at the 04/08 bilateral approach. #3 and #8 would move to round 1 and #2 would become Target sale decision. Rounds would renumber and counts would be unchanged.

Questions.Question: Cohort counts (gap in the source). The contact total of 50 includes 'CSC and Pamplona', which may be one party or two. The 16 unnamed financial NDA signers signed 'over the next two months' after 06/24, so some may have signed after the 07/23 due date.
Questions.Recommended answer: Contact remainder: Count blank, 47-48. NDA cohort: Count 16 (exact: 18 financial less B and C). Close all 16 with one inferred Did not submit row by 07/23, Count blank, saying up to 16 missed the deadline.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 31-32 give the totals and the 15/35 and 2/18 splits. Party A signed on 08/05 and is counted within the two months (p. 34), so NDA dates spread past 07/23. On 07/25 the advancing set was the four named bidders (p. 34).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If some of the 16 signed after 07/25, E14 would close them as Not selected at signing by 10/14 rather than Did not submit by 07/23. Live units in rounds 2-3 would then rise by an unknown number.

Questions.Question: Round 1 deadline outcome (choice of convention). The due date was 07/23/2013. Only CSC/Pamplona submitted on time; Party B (07/24) and Party C (07/24 oral, 07/25 written) were late, and both were reviewed on 07/25.
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). The Deadline set date is bounded 06/24-06/28 (first dated package delivery 06/28).
Questions.Why, with page: Bids and dates are on p. 33. On 07/25 BofA reviewed the indications of B, C and CSC/Pamplona and Party A's 06/21 proposal (p. 33), and all advanced (p. 34). No new date was set.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If late bids are not treated as responses the solicitation required, the outcome would be Enforced. The bidder set would not change.

Questions.Question: Round 2 deadline outcome (choice of convention). The due date was 09/09/2013. CSC/Pamplona and Party B were on time; Party A and Party C submitted on 09/10, and all four were reviewed on 09/11.
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: The letter set 'no later than September 9, 2013' (p. 35). Party A's and Party C's bids came on 09/10, and the 09/11 meeting reviewed all four (p. 35). No new date was set for round 2.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If Enforced, Party A's and Party C's 09/10 bids would read as outside the solicitation. Nothing else moves.

Questions.Question: Financing coding (permitted inference). Party A proposed funding from 'outstanding credit facilities or affiliated equity sources' with no firm commitment. Party B's 09/18 financing is known only from the committee's 09/19 remark.
Questions.Recommended answer: Party A and Party C on 09/10: Contingent (Heavy H1), since the source is reported and a commitment is expressly absent. Party A's 09/18 reiteration carries #35's terms. Party B 09/18: Contingent, Inferred = Y.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 35: 'Neither Party A's nor Party C's revised indication of interest included a firm financing commitment.' p. 37: Party B 'would likely be financing' with affiliated equity and third-party debt, riskier than Pamplona's funding.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Reading existing facilities as Not needed would give Party A Unclear rather than Heavy. Coding Party B 09/18 Not stated would give Unclear. Neither changes Formality.

Questions.Question: Round 3 deadline outcome (choice of convention). The due date was 09/18/2013. Three bidders responded on the day; Party C did not. On 09/19 the committee chose CSC/Pamplona and then invited it to improve.
Questions.Recommended answer: Enforced. The later $21.25 request is bargaining within the round.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 36 gives the 09/18 bids and Party C's non-submission. p. 37: on 09/19 the committee acted on the bids in hand, then set the $21.25 requirement with no new due date.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the $21.25 invitation were read as a new solicitation, a round 4 (exclusive negotiation) would open on 09/19-09/21 and #45-#63 would move to it.

Questions.Question: Formality of round-3 and exclusivity-period CSC/Pamplona bids (choice of convention). The final request asked for 'final indications of interest', and no markup existed before 09/25. Should these bids be Formal?
Questions.Recommended answer: Formal. #39-#41 answer a genuine final solicitation (route 2). #46-#47 answer the target's final-round price requirement ('last and best'). #55 and #57 are markups of the commitment letter (route 1). Prices on #55 and #57 are carried at $21.25.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 36: 'request final indications of interest' with exclusivity for one bidder. p. 37: 'last and best offer'. p. 39: redrafted commitment letter and cap proposal. The price was $21.25 at 09/21 and at signing, and exclusivity ended on any adverse change (pp. 37-38).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: The Informal reading (indications only, no documents) would make every pre-signing bid Informal. The comparison of the final round with signing would change for the estimation.

Questions.Question: Party A's 09/18 reiteration (choice of convention): Bid or Bid reaffirmed?
Questions.Recommended answer: Bid (a new communication answering the final solicitation), with price and terms carried from #35.
Questions.Why, with page: Bid reaffirmed needs the target to have moved to finalize an agreement with the bidder (E10), which it had not with Party A. The filing says it 'reiterated' that its previous indication 'was its best and final offer' (p. 36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If no row were recorded, Party A would have no round-3 bid, and Bids received in round 3 would drop to 2.

Questions.Question: Party B's 09/18 options (choice of convention): contingent consideration or stock?
Questions.Recommended answer: CVR/earnout Y with value $2.50 (Party B's own valuation). Upfront price $19.00, Stock % 0.
Questions.Why, with page: Options on 10% of new equity vest on achieving base-case projections over five years (p. 36): a performance-dependent security paid after closing. Party B valued them at $2.50 and the package at $21.50 (p. 36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Treating the options as stock would give a Part stock or $21.50 package price and make Party B's bid look higher than CSC/Pamplona's $20.75 on an upfront basis.

Questions.Question: Regulatory coding for the CSC/Pamplona final proposal (permitted inference). A $15M reverse termination fee was payable if regulatory clearance failed. Is that a reported regulatory concern?
Questions.Recommended answer: Not stated, with the fee recorded in the Note. The background reports no expected obstacle; the fee allocates risk.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 37: fee 'in the event regulatory clearance is not obtained'. The merger agreement ties the fee to antitrust conditions (pp. 80-81), but that date is 10/14. HSR expired without a second request on 11/27/2013 (p. 85).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Coding Concern (Antitrust Y) would flag antitrust risk on CSC/Pamplona's final bids. Conditions stay Light, since Concern alone is not H3.

Questions.Question: Exits of Party A and Party B (permitted inference). Neither is mentioned after the 09/19 meeting. Should both be dropped at the exclusivity execution, and with which reasons?
Questions.Recommended answer: Dropped by target by 09/24/2013, Inferred = Y. Party A: Would not improve earlier offer (it declared $18-19 best and final). Party B: Terms or process (options and financing risk).
Questions.Why, with page: E14: a live rival at the execution of exclusivity with another bidder is dropped. p. 36: Party A called its offer best and final. p. 37: the committee preferred CSC/Pamplona on value, certainty and risk.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Dating the exits to the 09/19 selection instead would move them before #45. Coding Party A as Lower offer than rivals would change its exit-reason statistics.

Deal facts.Value: Mac-Gray Corporation

CSC ServiceWorks, Inc. (with CSC ServiceWorks Holdings, Inc.; buyer Spin Holdco Inc. and merger sub CSC Fenway, Inc.), a portfolio company of Pamplona Capital Partners III, L.P., which committed the equity ("CSC/Pamplona")

Strategic: CSC is a laundry-services operating company owned by the sponsor Pamplona, and the filing calls CSC/Pamplona a strategic bidder (p. 32). Pamplona funded the price through a $594M commitment letter.
$21.25 per share in cash (no stock, no contingent payment)
10/15/2013 (before U.S. market open)
target-led (the Board had BofA approach Party A on 04/08/2013; Party A made an unsolicited proposal on 06/21/2013; the Special Committee launched a broad auction on 06/24/2013)

None reported for a sale of Mac-Gray. The filing mentions transactions discussed "from time to time" with CSC and other industry participants, and the 2011-2012 Discussions on Mac-Gray acquiring CSC (BofA engaged 10/23/2012). CSC then ran its own sale process and was bought by Pamplona in May 2013 (p. 27).
Met (process 1): 20 parties (Party A, CSC/Pamplona and 18 financial parties including Party B and Party C)
Yes

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per share
BofA Merrill Lynch (engaged 05/30-05/31/2013; earlier buy-side engagement from 10/23/2012 ended 05/15/2013)
Goodwin Procter LLP

After BofA Merrill Lynch sounded out strategic rival Party A in April 2013, Party A made an unsolicited $17-19 cash proposal on 06/21/2013. On 06/24 a newly formed Special Committee launched an auction, contacting 50 parties, of which 20 signed confidentiality agreements. CSC/Pamplona, Party B and Party C gave preliminary indications of $15-18.50 around the 07/23 deadline. The committee advanced them and Party A to management meetings and staged diligence, which gave the strategic bidders less customer data. Revised bids of 09/09-09/10 ran from $16 to $19.50. At the 09/18 final deadline CSC/Pamplona bid $20.75, Party B $19.00 cash plus options it valued at $2.50, and Party A held at $18-19, while Party C dropped out. The committee preferred CSC/Pamplona's fully Pamplona-funded offer and required $21.25, which CSC/Pamplona accepted for exclusivity from 09/24. After agreeing a $50M cap on Pamplona's liability and an $11M target termination fee, the parties signed on 10/14/2013 at $21.25 in cash.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: where do the process and round boundaries fall?
Questions.Recommended answer: One process starts April 5; rounds open June 24, July 25 and September 11. June 21 Party A bid is round 0. July 25 Party C written revision answers round 1.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 27–41. E5: (a) no break with all bids/participants closed; (b) no ~3-month sale-contact gap; (c) no fresh restart. No interval of about two months without reported acquirer contact. No supported alternative process or round boundary; Party C’s July 25 written revision could instead be assigned to round 2.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative shifts early events and Party C revision across round boundaries.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: what happened at July 23 preliminary bid deadline?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted); July 24 B and C submissions entered July 25 comparison.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 32–34. No replacement due date was set; late responses required by the solicitation were considered. Party A had no NDA by July 23 and was not a timely respondent.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would treat the late submissions as post-cutoff bargaining rather than accepted responses.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: when did the 16 unnamed financial NDA parties enter, and when did they leave?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep the exact residual count 16; date its collective entry across the reported two-month period and infer closure by August 27, without saying all were eligible July 23.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 32 gives 20 NDAs, two strategic and 18 financial; pp. 34–35 name only four selected for later diligence and revised bids. Individual NDA and exit dates are absent, so July 25 cannot be an exact collective exit date.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If some signed after August 27 or stayed in reserve, the collective exit timing and live-count map change; individual rows would be needed.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: what happened at September 9 revised proposal deadline?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted); Party A and C responded September 10 and committee reviewed all four September 11.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 35. The September 9 letter asked for written revisions; Party C instead responded orally. No replacement due date is stated, but the late proposals were considered.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would classify the September 10 bids as post-cutoff negotiations; only two would be timely.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: what happened at September 18 final indication deadline and to Party C?
Questions.Recommended answer: Enforced for the deadline; Party C Did not submit and left the whole-company contest on September 18.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 36–37. The banker asked all four for final indications; three answered September 18. Party C neither revised nor reaffirmed and gave no reason. Committee reviewed bids in hand September 19.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A softer deadline or open Party C status would alter the final-round live bidder count.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how should CSC price revisions, later document work and reaffirmation be classified?
Questions.Recommended answer: September 21 and September 21–23 revisions are Informal; October 7 buyer markup formally reaffirms $21.25. October 5/8 liability revisions have blank price absent express incorporation.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 37–40. The final September 18 response is Formal under the final solicitation. Subsequent price-only negotiation and sponsor-letter revision have no independent markup route until Kirkland returned a revised merger agreement October 7. The reverse fee on pp. 37–38 records a regulatory risk, without making it an H3 condition.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A broader carry-forward reading would mark later bids Formal or fill more terms; treating the reverse fee as a routine approval term would change Regulatory to Not stated.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: what part of Party B’s $21.50 package was upfront, and what were its options?
Questions.Recommended answer: Record $19 cash upfront and $2.50 contingent option value attributed to Party B; stock share 0%. Financing at the bid date is Not stated.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 36 says options vest over five years on base projections and Party B valued them at $2.50 incremental value per share. Their performance-based deferred payoff meets contingent consideration convention. The p. 37 committee discussion of likely third-party debt occurred the next day and does not date financing commitment status to September 18.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Treating options as upfront stock would inflate immediate consideration and change comparison with CSC cash bid.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: how did Party A and Party B leave after CSC exclusivity?
Questions.Recommended answer: Infer both Dropped by target by the September 24 execution, with Exit reason Not stated.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 38 reports executed CSC/Pamplona exclusivity. E14 closes live rivals at that transition. p. 37 discusses offer comparisons but does not explicitly assign an exclusion reason to either rival.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If either remained in reserve despite exclusivity, its participation would stay open until a later reported closure or signing.

In April 2013 Mac-Gray began exploring transactions and contacted Party A, which made an unsolicited cash offer in June. The Special Committee then solicited 50 parties; 20 signed confidentiality agreements and three other named bidders made preliminary offers. Four bidders received staged diligence and were asked for revised proposals and then final indications. Party C did not respond in the final stage, while the committee favored CSC/Pamplona over Party A and Party B despite Party B’s higher stated package value. CSC/Pamplona raised its cash price to $21.25, received exclusivity, and signed on October 14; the merger was announced October 15.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: process and round boundaries, including the 04/08/2013–06/21/2013 contact gap?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep one process: R1 06/24 outreach mandate; R2 07/25 selected diligence/revised bids; R3 09/11 final solicitation. Alternative R2 on 08/27 moves intervening R2 rows to R1, but duplicates a stage already opened.
Questions.Why, with page: Only sale-contact gap about two months: 04/08–06/21 (74 days). E5(a) fails: Party A kept in view; (b) fails: less than about three months, no termination; (c) met: June fresh outreach. Earlier 2011–2012 talks concerned target buying CSC, not its sale (pp. 27–34, 36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative shifts #28, #29, #31, #32, #33 to the preliminary stage and dates R2 to #34. No supported extra process.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention / source gap: July 23 round-1 deadline outcome and Party A’s standing proposal?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). Count three fresh round-1 bidders: CSC/Pamplona, B and C. A’s June proposal remained under review; no July submission or reaffirmation is invented.
Questions.Why, with page: B and C first bid July 24; July 25 committee considered both and CSC plus A’s June bid. A’s NDA remained unresolved and it continued, so no missed-deadline exit (pp. 32–34).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would discard accepted late responses. Treating A’s standing proposal as a new bid raises R1 distinct bidders from three to four without a reported new communication.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: September 9 round-2 deadline outcome?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted); four revised bidders. A and C remained in without exits or re-entry.
Questions.Why, with page: September 9 written bids requested; A’s and C’s responses arrived September 10, C orally. All four were reviewed September 11 and invited to final stage (pp. 35–36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced understates accepted lateness; excluding C for missing written form reduces observed bidders incorrectly.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: September 18 final-round deadline and later CSC price increase?
Questions.Recommended answer: Enforced. Three final bidders; C did not submit. Target’s September 21 invited price improvement is bargaining within R3, with no new due date.
Questions.Why, with page: Target evaluated final responses September 19 and proposed $21.25 on September 21. No unsolicited overdue required response accepted (pp. 36–37). Exclusivity dates are not bid deadlines.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Calling deadline extended would confuse invited bargaining with a late response; an extra round would move CSC’s final negotiations and signing unnecessarily.

Questions.Question: Source gap / permitted inference: when did the 16 anonymous financial NDA signers leave?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep exact residual 16, but no exact July 23 non-submitter count. Infer Dropped by target by September 11 final four-party selection, after the full NDA window. Actual exits may precede this bound.
Questions.Why, with page: 20 NDAs over two months after June 24: 2 strategic and 18 financial, including B/C. July 25 advancement names four, but unknown residual execution dates prevent assigning all 16 to that transition (pp. 32–36).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If all 16 were eligible July 23, close them Did not submit then; if live July 25, drop them then. Stage-2 process-wide live count changes; four named admitted bidders and total 20 entrants do not.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: are Party B’s performance-vesting options stock or contingent consideration?
Questions.Recommended answer: Code $19 upfront cash, Stock % = 0, CVR/earnout = Y and value $2.50 (Party B’s valuation, not guaranteed payout). Retain bidder-stated $21.50 package in Note.
Questions.Why, with page: Options represent 10% new equity, with strike at B’s initial cost; vest on five-year base projections excluding acquisitions. E13 treats performance-dependent securities as contingent payments (pp. 36–37).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Treating options as upfront stock overstates comparable certain price; the option valuation is not a guaranteed face payment or maximum.

Questions.Question: Source gap / choice of convention: classify late CSC commitment revisions and unstated carried terms?
Questions.Recommended answer: Record September 21–23 reverse fee and October 5/8 sponsor-cap revisions as separate Formal bids. Leave October price/consideration blank or Not stated: the communications do not expressly carry a price. Signing retains $21.25 cash.
Questions.Why, with page: Reverse fee $15m; sponsor cap initially unspecified then $50m (pp. 37–40). E10 requires material commitment rows and date-specific terms. Light reflects committed funding or only confirmatory diligence/final documentation; no substantive diligence period reported.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Carrying standing $21.25 fills missing October prices but requires inference; omitting revisions loses bidder commitment changes. Extending open diligence to September 21–23 would make its Conditions Unclear.

Questions.Question: Source gap / permitted inference: classify initiation, bidder types and Party A’s earliest contact?
Questions.Recommended answer: Target-led initiation. April 5 is preliminary transactional exploration; keep April 8 as Target interest and June 21 as A’s first whole-company Bid. CSC/Pamplona is Strategic: operating-company acquisition with sponsor funding; Moab rollover creates no additional bidder.
Questions.Why, with page: April business-combination roles were unspecified; the June proposal clearly purchases Mac-Gray. Target began strategic review before Moab’s proxy victory; no sale demand reported. CSC is operating buyer, Pamplona its sponsor (pp. 26–32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: An unresolved-scope reading changes April event label, not entry date. Mixed or Financial buyer type misclassifies sponsor-funded operating acquisition. Activist-influenced initiation is not established by the filing.

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: USD per Mac-Gray common share (merger agreement currency definition p. A-9). Party B final upfront price $19; contingent options valued by Party B at $2.50/share are separate from its $21.50 package. Liability/fee amounts in Notes are total USD.
BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated); original mandate 10/23/2012 ended 05/15/2013; fresh engagement approved 05/30, letter 05/31/2013 (pp. 27, 29–30).
Goodwin Procter LLP, acting by 05/09/2013 (p. 27).

Mac-Gray explored strategic alternatives and approached Party A before organizing a broader sale process in June 2013. The target contacted 50 prospective buyers and eventually signed confidentiality agreements with 20, although the filing does not place every anonymous signer before the first deadline. Four named bidders advanced to staged diligence, and all four were invited to submit final indications in September. Party C did not submit a final response; Party B offered $19 cash plus performance-dependent options that it valued at $2.50, while CSC/Pamplona offered $20.75 cash. Mac-Gray negotiated CSC/Pamplona up to $21.25 cash, executed exclusivity, and settled sponsor funding and liability terms. The parties signed on October 14 and announced on October 15, with no later competing offer or go-shop reported in the filing.

Mac-Gray's board began exploring strategic alternatives in spring 2013, had BofA Merrill Lynch sound out strategic rival Party A in April, and received an unsolicited $17-19 cash proposal from Party A on June 21. On June 24 a Special Committee of independent directors launched an auction, approaching 50 parties (15 strategic, 35 financial); 20 signed NDAs and CSC/Pamplona, Party B and Party C submitted preliminary indications in late July. The committee advanced four bidders, adding Party A once it signed an NDA, to management meetings and staged diligence that held back customer data from the strategic bidders, and received revised indications of $16-19.50 on September 9-10. In a final round due September 18, CSC/Pamplona bid $20.75 with full Pamplona funding, Party B offered $19.00 cash plus performance options it valued at $2.50, Party A stood at $18-19 and Party C dropped out. The committee chose CSC/Pamplona, which raised to $21.25 as its last and best offer in return for exclusivity, executed September 24 and extended to October 15. After agreeing a $50 million cap on Pamplona's liability and an $11 million target termination fee, the parties signed on October 14, 2013 and announced the deal on October 15.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: where should process and round boundaries fall?
Questions.Recommended answer: One continuing process; round 1 opens March 24, round 2 June 1, round 3 July 27. No supported alternative process boundary.
Questions.Why, with page: E5(a) fails: Party A remained in view; (b) is unresolved because the Q4 meeting day is unknown; (c) the March board decision is a fresh start. The reported acquirer-contact gap is at least Dec. 31, 2015–Mar. 22, 2016 (possibly longer because the Q4 Party A meeting is undated). March 24 outreach authorization was executed within a week (pp. 27–32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Opening round 1 at first outreach in the week of March 28 would change row 5 and its Rounds Opened date; the other rows would retain their rounds.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: did the May 10 IOI deadline arrive before extension, and what happened at the May 19 cutoff?
Questions.Recommended answer: Treat May 10 as superseded with unknown revision day; code May 19 outcome Unclear.
Questions.Why, with page: The filing says the May 10 date was “subsequently postponed” to May 19 but does not date the change. It gives only a May 19–June 1 window for nine IOIs, so a late submission is possible but not established (p. 29).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: May 10 could need a Deadline row and outcome; proved post-May-19 IOIs would change outcome to Extended (late bid accepted).

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: how did the July 20 LOI deadline operate?
Questions.Recommended answer: Code Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: G&W submitted its requested LOI July 21; the committee reviewed LOIs July 22 and July 27, considered G&W, and continued with it (pp. 29–30). No new due date is reported.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If July 20 was treated as soft, outcome would be Passed without action; the late accepted G&W response supports the recommended code.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: which later-named parties belonged to the original outreach and NDA cohorts?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep the 11 strategic and 18 financial outreach totals, the 25 initial NDA signers, and Party C’s later NDA separate; avoid assigning B, D, E, F to individual initial NDA dates. Count G&W’s April 3 NDA once.
Questions.Why, with page: Party A is expressly within the 11, and Annex A dates G&W’s NDA April 3; the background does not identify all named parties in the initial cohort or establish the exact eligibility set for the May IOI request (pp. 28–29; Annex A p. A-48).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A proven mapping could change the initial strategic NDA residual, Round 1 membership, and inferred non-submitter count.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: did Party F’s August 1 financing support make it a joint bidder with Party E or establish committed financing?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Party E as the bidder; classify its funding Not stated and describe Party F’s support in the Note.
Questions.Why, with page: The filing calls Party F’s role “financing support” and gives neither an equity offer by F nor binding funding terms (p. 30). E4 treats financing support alone as insufficient to create a bidding group.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A joint offer would reduce or change bidder-unit counts; binding financing evidence could change Financing and Conditions.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: is Party B’s August 4 returned merger draft a bid reaffirmation?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes: record a Formal reaffirmation of the standing $24 bid.
Questions.Why, with page: The company had decided to complete the agreement with B and B’s counsel returned a revised merger draft. E10 permits reaffirmation by a bidder’s own markup after movement to finalization when its priced row sat in a non-final round (pp. 30–31).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Omitting it would remove the formal offer confirmation during the final negotiation stage.

Party A’s late-2015 interest in a joint venture and equity investment prompted a banker search. In March 2016 the board began a change-of-control exploration and GHF contacted 29 potential buyers. Nine initial IOIs led to seven parties advancing to presentations and diligence, with Party C joining later. Six LOIs arrived; the committee narrowed definitive negotiations to Party B and G&W while later revisions from Parties D and E were considered. G&W replaced its cash-plus-CVR bid with a $25 all-cash offer on August 12, and Party B declined to improve its $24 offer. The company signed with G&W that day and announced the merger August 15.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: where do processes and rounds begin?
Questions.Recommended answer: One process; round 1 opens 03/24 outreach authorization, round 2 at seven-bidder advancement (05/23–06/01), round 3 at G&W/Party B definitive negotiation (by 07/27).
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 27–31. Only long pre-signing contact gap: Q4 2015 Party A meeting (10/01–12/31) to 03/22/2016, about 82–173 days. E5(a) fails: Party A kept in view; (b) uncertain: endpoint spans below/above three months, no termination; (c) met: fresh board mandate/outreach. Thus no new process.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Plausible alternative: round 1 opens 03/28 actual outreach, moving 03/24 authorization/legal row to round 0; same bidders/bids. Treating June document-markup stage as already final would merge round 3 into round 2 and remove B’s reaffirmation. Recommend distinct later definitive stage: no final solicitation in June.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / permitted inference: when was 05/10 extended, and what happened at 05/19?
Questions.Recommended answer: Assume 05/10 superseded before arrival; no Deadline row. Record 05/19 as Extended (late bid accepted), with nine receipts reported over 05/19–06/01.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 29 does not date postponement or identify individual receipt days. Extension window is retained broadly; no day of actual communication asserted. Receipt interval supports accepted lateness without inventing a replacement deadline.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If extension followed 05/10, add a 05/10 Deadline with Extended and reorder revision. If all nine arrived 05/19, change that outcome to Enforced or Unclear; bid dates remain interval-valued.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / choice of convention: was the 07/20 LOI deadline enforced?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). Six LOIs received in late July, including G&W on 07/21; its invited price revision on 07/26 remains in round 2. No new due date.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 29–30. Two bidders elected not to submit. Other bidders’ arrival days are unstated; late-July window ends at 07/27 committee review. G&W’s 08/13 offer expiry is not a target bid deadline.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would require evidence that the target used 07/20 as a cutoff despite considering required late submissions. No supported alternative; keep exits separate from lateness.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: reconcile NDA totals, extra contacts, and anonymous cohort membership.
Questions.Recommended answer: Retain 11 strategic + 14 financial initial NDA signers and separately record late Party C. Detailed chronology implies at least 26; flag conflicting 25-total summary. Preserve anonymous residual as a bound, not exact 16.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 28 gives original 29 contacts/25 NDAs and two additional Class I contacts; p. 29 expressly calls C new. p. 33 says 25 total. Nine IOIs/seven advanced/six LOIs are exact; membership of other named buyers in original outreach is not expressly allocated.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Resolving original-cohort membership can reduce residual 16–24 to 16 and establish exact process-wide unique count. Detailed NDA chronology takes priority over summary; auction screen Met either way. Extra contacts alone generate no bidder entries or exits.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / choice of convention: did Party A initially bid, and which anonymous exit includes it?
Questions.Recommended answer: Initial JV/equity interest is an Other material event, not an established acquisition proposal. Party A enters whole-company outreach/NDA cohort later. Keep it within unresolved anonymous exits, not a duplicate named exit.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 27–30. Party A’s early scope is unresolved; March outreach concerns a change of control. Its later identity could be a non-IOI bidder, one of two low bidders, or the strategic LOI non-submitter.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If early language is treated as a proposal, use Other-scope bid with no per-share price. If identity is resolved, split the corresponding anonymous exit and reduce its residual; never add another bidder or exit.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention / permitted inference: how should returning D/E and financing supporter F be counted?
Questions.Recommended answer: D and E re-enter 07/29 after target exclusion. F supplies financing only; no re-entry or group change. E’s 08/02 reversion keeps its original offer live; infer Not selected at signing. D withdraws over exclusivity.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 30 expressly describes exclusion, reengagement, Party F financing support, and E confirming its original proposal. Only G&W and B were admitted to final diligence; D/E proposals still received.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Calling E’s revised-offer withdrawal a bidder withdrawal would close its participation too early. Treating F as a joint acquirer would require a group-change row; support alone does not establish one. No support for readmitting D/E to finalist stage.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: does Party B’s 08/04 markup earn Bid reaffirmed?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes: standing $24 price carried from initial LOI under E10; its own revised agreement returned after target moved to finalize with it. Latest priced row was in a Not final round even though Formal.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 29, 31. E10 permits reaffirmation when prior priced bid was Informal OR in Not final round. The markup’s other terms/status are not presumed unchanged.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Omitting this row removes Party B from round 3 Bids received and leaves its last priced row in round 2. If round 2 is classified final, omit reaffirmation as redundant.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how should revised LOIs and incomplete condition evidence be coded?
Questions.Recommended answer: Formal when contemporaneous definitive markups appear (B/D/G&W July LOIs; G&W 08/12). Price-only revised LOIs without express incorporation default Informal. Keep unknown terms unknown; Party E’s combined 60-day exclusivity period alone is not H2.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 29–31. G&W 07/26 and D 08/01 lack new markups/incorporation. E expressly reverts original proposal 08/02. G&W only explicitly completes physical diligence; no all-diligence-complete statement. Signing financing assurances (p. 34; A-22) postdate morning offer.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Broader carry-forward would change formality/exclusivity/condition labels for revisions. Treating combined exclusivity as a diligence period changes E to Heavy; treating physical completion as all diligence complete changes G&W. Recommend evidence-at-date coding.

Deal facts.Value: mixed — Party A preliminary equity/JV interest prompted review; target initiated broader whole-company outreach.
None reported outside this process. Q4 2015 Party A commercial/JV/equity discussion retained as round 0 context (p. 27).

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per common share, assuming preferred conversion. G&W early CVR excluded from upfront Price low/high; stated $1.13 per share shown separately. Equity-value equivalents remain in Notes.
Greene Holcomb & Fisher LLC (GHF), retained 01/27/2016; business acquired by BMO Capital Markets Corp. on 08/01/2016 (pp. 27, 30). One continuing advisory relationship.
Hinckley, Allen & Snyder LLP (first shown acting 03/24/2016, p. 28); unnamed STB counsel (08/12/2016, p. 32).

Party A’s preliminary joint-venture and equity interest in late 2015 led PWRR to consider a broader sale. GHF organized March 2016 outreach to 29 potential buyers, and the detailed background reports 25 initial NDA signers. Nine initial IOIs led to seven bidders advancing to diligence, after which late entrant Party C joined and six bidders submitted LOIs. The target selected G&W and Party B for definitive negotiations; Party D and Party E returned with revisions, but D stopped over exclusivity and E reverted to its original offer. G&W raised its offer to $25 cash on August 12, Party B declined to improve $24, and PWRR signed with G&W that day and announced the transaction August 15. The filing leaves NDA totals and some anonymous bidder identities unresolved, as explained in Questions.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: where do the process and rounds begin, especially the July definitive stage?
Questions.Recommended answer: One process, three rounds: 03/24 outreach authorization; 05/23–06/01 selection of seven; 07/22–07/27 selection of two for definitive negotiation. Round 3 Inferred final. Q4-2015 equity/JV interest is preliminary, not a whole-company offer.
Questions.Why, with page: Only ≥about-two-month contact gap: Party A meeting in 10/01–12/31/2015 to 03/22/2016 (82–173 days). E5(a) fails: Party A carried forward; (b) ≥3 months indeterminate, no reported termination; (c) fresh March decision/outreach yes. All three do not hold (pp. 27–31).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Plausible alternative delays round 3 to 08/04 explicit instruction to finalize Party B, moving #41–#52 to round 2 and opening round 3 at #53. Earlier selection plus 08/01 and 08/03 revised agreements favors current map. No supported new-process boundary.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / permitted timing inference: what happened to round-1 IOI due dates?
Questions.Recommended answer: Treat 05/10 as superseded before arrival (inferred); record 05/19 as Extended (late bid accepted). Preserve revision window through 05/19; no individual timely/late assignments.
Questions.Why, with page: 04/27 report states May 10 was subsequently postponed to May 19; exact extension day unreported. Nine IOIs received May 19–June 1 and evaluated (pp. 28–29).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If May 10 was reached while operative, add its Deadline row and an Extended outcome before the May 19 late-acceptance outcome; reorder the revision after that deadline. Bid and live counts unchanged.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: was the round-2 July 20 cutoff enforced?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). No further due date reported. G&W’s July 21 first LOI answers this solicitation; retain participation without exit/re-entry.
Questions.Why, with page: LOIs due July 20; G&W first LOI expressly July 21. Six LOIs described as late July; reviews July 22 and July 27. Two unnamed bidders elected not to submit (pp. 29–30).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Enforced would require treating the accepted July 21 response as outside the July 20 solicitation, unsupported here. Other LOI arrival days remain windows; no deadline-based exact exit dates.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / population reconciliation: are there 25 or 26 NDA acquirers, and where does Party A exit?
Questions.Recommended answer: Use detailed 25 initial signers (11 Strategic, 14 Financial) plus new Party C = 26; flag p. 33’s total 25. Keep later continuing names inside initial cohorts; do not add two contact-only railroads. Keep Party A inside unidentified residual cohorts, without a duplicate exit.
Questions.Why, with page: March outreach/NDAs and two additional contacts p. 28; nine IOIs, seven advanced and new Party C p. 29; six LOIs plus two non-submitters p. 30. Page 33 says 25 overall. Party A could be among 16 non-advancers, two low IOIs, or unnamed Strategic LOI non-submitter. Its location is unresolved.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A literal inclusive total 25 reduces initial cohort/residual closure by one, with no supported type allocation. If named bidders/additional railroads were outside original cohorts, totals and residuals require bounds. Recommended live progression: 25 → 7 → 8 → 6 → 2 → 4 → 3 → 1 winner; residual closure timing is inferred at advancement, not May 19.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: does markup-backed formality carry into later price revisions, and does Party E’s 60-day exclusivity imply Heavy diligence?
Questions.Recommended answer: Formal: original B, D and G&W LOIs, plus G&W August 12 markup-backed bid. G&W July 26 and D/E August 1 revisions remain Informal without renewed markup/incorporation. Party E initial/reverted offer Unclear: 60 days is a mixed exclusivity period, not stated diligence duration.
Questions.Why, with page: Markups and issues summary distinguished p. 29. Revised communications and 30-day requirements p. 30. E11 assesses each communication; E12 does not equate exclusivity duration with diligence duration.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A broader document-continuity reading makes later revisions Formal. Treating Party E’s entire exclusivity period as diligence makes initial/reverted offers Heavy (H2). Price, round and participation counts do not change.

Questions.Question: Gap in source / choice of convention: how complete and committed was G&W’s final morning offer?
Questions.Recommended answer: Formal, Conditions Unclear, Due diligence Incomplete, Financing and Regulatory Not stated at submission. Only physical diligence is expressly completed; do not infer all diligence finished or backdate signing representations.
Questions.Why, with page: Physical diligence completed August 11 and final LOI/markups morning August 12 (p. 31). Board STB comparison later that day (p. 32). No financing condition and sufficient funds are signing disclosures (pp. 34, A-22).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If same-day signing assurances are treated as contemporaneous bid evidence, Financing becomes Committed and regulatory assurance/risk may be coded. Conditions become Light or None only with additional supported readiness/diligence judgment; no earlier bid changes.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference / choice of convention: did Party E exit August 2, or form a joint bidder with Party F?
Questions.Recommended answer: Neither. August 2 is a Bid reverting to the original $21.26 proposal; retain E until inferred Not selected at signing. Party F is financing support only, not a joint acquirer or independent re-entry.
Questions.Why, with page: E confirms original proposal while withdrawing revised proposal; F described solely as financing support (p. 30). Signing with G&W closes E’s outstanding participation (p. 32). E4/E10/E14 apply.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Reading August 2 as full withdrawal reduces live competitors after that day from three to two. Treating F as joint acquirer would require a Bidding group changed row and different participant genealogy, without an additional independent bidder.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: should Party B’s August 4 returned merger draft count as a priced reaffirmation?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes: Bid reaffirmed at standing $24, Formal, with contemporary conditions coded separately. E10 applies because its latest priced proposal was in round 2, which is Not final, and target moved to finalize with B before receiving B’s draft.
Questions.Why, with page: August 4 target instruction prioritizes completing B’s agreement; B’s counsel returns its own revised draft the same day (p. 31). Standing $24 originates in the LOI (p. 29) and remains the compared price on August 12 (p. 32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If treated as routine document exchange, remove the reaffirmation and reduce round-3 distinct bidding units from four to three; B remains a live admitted bidder. No change to cash/stock, financing or diligence facts is inferred.

Greene Holcomb & Fisher LLC; business acquired by BMO Capital Markets Corp. on 08/01/2016, continuing relationship (pp. 27, 30, 41).
Hinckley, Allen & Snyder LLP; unnamed STB counsel also consulted on 08/12 (pp. 28, 32).

Party A’s late-2015 interest in a joint venture or equity investment led PWRR to hire GHF and organize a broad sale process in March 2016. The detailed background reports 25 initial NDA signers, nine IOIs and seven bidders selected for further diligence, followed by late entrant Party C. Six bidders submitted LOIs, and G&W and Party B were selected for definitive negotiations after the July deadline. Parties D and E re-entered, but D withdrew over diligence protection and E reverted to its original offer; Party F supplied financing support to E without becoming a joint bidder. After PWRR prioritized Party B, G&W raised its cash-and-CVR offer to $25 entirely in cash, and Party B declined to improve its $24 offer. PWRR signed with G&W on August 12 and announced the merger August 15; the filing leaves a 25-versus-26 NDA discrepancy and several timing and condition details unresolved.

Questions.Question: Gap in the source: Party A's Q4 2015 interest was in joint ventures and 'acquiring equity', with no stake size or proposal. Record it as Bidder interest (round 0, no entry), as a partial-scope matter, or as a whole-company approach?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Bidder interest in round 0 with scope unresolved. Party A enters only through the March 2016 NDA cohort (#9); its later fate stays inside the anonymous cohorts.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 27: Party A 'expressed some interest in acquiring equity in the Company'; no price or proposal. p. 28: Party A is named among the 11 strategic buyers contacted and later received the memorandum, then is never mentioned again.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Read as a whole-company approach, initiation becomes bidder-led. Read as partial, #1 becomes an Other material event. Counts are unaffected.

Questions.Question: Process and round map (choice of convention): one process with three rounds. R1, the IOI stage, from 03/24/2016; R2, the LOI stage, from the 05/23–06/01 admission of seven; R3, definitive negotiation with G&W and Party B, from the 07/22–07/27 selection.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep. Most plausible alternatives: (i), the most plausible, fold R3 into R2, treating the selection as how R2 ended: #39 is removed, #44–#65 move to round 2, and R2 becomes Inferred final; (ii) date R3 at 07/22, which moves #37–#38 into round 3; (iii) open R1 at the 03/14 decision, which moves #4 into round 1.
Questions.Why, with page: E6: moving to definitive negotiation with selected bidders after a non-final LOI round opens a round (p. 30). R3 is sorted at 07/27 because G&W's $21.15 LOI was below E's $21.26, so the 'higher offers' finding implies G&W's 07/26 revision had arrived. Gap of about two months or more with no acquirer contact: Q4 2015 (#1, 10/01–12/31/2015) to 03/22/2016 (#4). E5: (a) not met, since the Board kept Party A in view (bankers hired for 'possible negotiations with Party A', p. 27); (b) the gap is 82–173 days but no attempt was reported ended; (c) met on 03/14. Result: one process.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: (i) changes round membership and finality for the D/E re-entries and the final bids; (ii) changes the round of G&W's 07/26 revision; (iii) changes only the round of #4.

Questions.Question: Gap in the source: the background gives 11 strategic + 14 financial NDA signers after the 03/28 outreach, plus Party C in July. G&W's NDA is dated 04/03 (Annex A) and Party B's is undated. The reasons section says 25 signed in all. Are G&W and B inside the 11, and how many signed?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep G&W and Party B as separate entries, since membership in the 11 is not established, with the overlap flagged. Record at least 26 NDA signers for the process, reading p. 33's 25 as the first-wave total.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 28: 'Each of the potential strategic buyers and 14 potential financial buyers subsequently executed confidentiality agreements'; p. 29: Party C 'had not previously been part of the process'; p. 33: '25 of whom entered into confidentiality agreements'; p. A-48: G&W NDA dated 04/03/2016.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If G&W and B are among the 11, recorded entries fall from 28 to 26, live bidders at the IOI deadline from 27 to 25, and IOI non-submitters (#20) from 18 to 16. The two Class I railroads (#13) would add entries if they signed.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcomes, round 1 (gap in the source): IOIs due 05/10, postponed to 05/19 (postponement date not stated); nine IOIs received 05/19–06/01.
Questions.Recommended answer: 05/10: superseded before arrival, so no outcome. 05/19: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: p. 29: the deadline was 'subsequently postponed to May 19, 2016 to ensure the potential buyers had sufficient time'; the 04/27 report still cited 05/10. IOIs arrived 'Between May 19, 2016 and June 1, 2016' and the Committee considered them on 05/23 and 06/01 without setting a new date.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the postponement came after 05/10, that date takes Extended. If all nine had arrived by 05/19, the 05/19 outcome becomes Enforced, since the Committee used the set to select seven.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: the nine IOI bidders and the seven admitted are unnamed. I infer that the seven were G&W, Parties B, D, E and F, one unnamed strategic and one unnamed financial buyer.
Questions.Recommended answer: Accept. Party A and the two excluded low bidders remain anonymous inside cohorts.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 29: after two were excluded, GHF told 'all potential buyers' to submit LOIs. pp. 29–30: six LOIs came in, including late entrant C, and 'One strategic buyer and one financial buyer elected not to submit an LOI', so 5 named + 2 = 7.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the LOI invitation reached parties outside the seven, some named LOI bidders may not have submitted IOIs or been admitted. That changes round-2 membership and the IOI cohort's type mix, and Party A could be the unnamed strategic non-submitter.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: were the IOIs (the nine, and Party C's) made before diligence began?
Questions.Recommended answer: Due diligence Not begun for both, because data-site access came only after each IOI.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 29: after the IOIs the Committee let the seven 'conduct additional due diligence' through a data site; Party C got data-site access 'Subsequently' to its 07/12 IOI. The word 'additional' suggests some earlier review of the memorandum.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If memorandum review and introductory meetings count as diligence access, these rows become Incomplete. The Conditions level (Unclear) does not change.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcome, round 2 (choice of convention): LOIs were due 07/20; G&W's arrived 07/21 and the others in 'late July'. The Committee reviewed them on 07/22 and 07/27.
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: p. 29: 'G&W submitted an LOI on July 21, 2016'; it was reviewed and G&W was later selected (p. 30). No new due date was set.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If G&W's one-day lateness is disregarded, the outcome is Enforced: the Committee used the LOIs to select G&W and B, and G&W's 07/26 improvement is bargaining. If the date is read as soft, Passed without action.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: Party E's LOI was 'subject to a 60-day exclusivity period for due diligence and negotiation of definitive documentation'. Is that an H2 diligence period, or only an exclusivity or negotiation period?
Questions.Recommended answer: Heavy (H2). The filing ties the period expressly to due diligence, as it does for the other LOIs' 30-day and four-week periods.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 30. E12 excludes a bare exclusivity or negotiation period from H2, but this one is stated to be for due diligence.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If read as exclusivity or negotiation only, #30 and #49 become Unclear (diligence open, no separate diligence period). Exclusivity stays Required.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: G&W's 07/26 revision and D's and E's 08/01 revisions report no mark-up and no reference back to earlier terms. Are they Informal?
Questions.Recommended answer: Informal. Under E11, a price-only revision is Formal only on its own or by express reference to earlier Formal terms.
Questions.Why, with page: pp. 29–30: 'revised LOI, which increased its offer'; 'revised LOI at a price of $24.00'. The Company's 08/03 drafts to G&W reflected G&W's July mark-ups (p. 30), but target negotiation from an earlier mark-up does not make a revision Formal.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If G&W's and D's July mark-ups are read as standing behind their revisions, #38 and #46 become Formal.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: Party E's confirmed $21.26 offer (08/02) is never mentioned again. When and how did E's participation end?
Questions.Recommended answer: Not selected at signing by 08/12/2016, Inferred, reason Not stated: its offer was still standing and no decision excluded it.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 30: E 'confirmed its original proposal of $21.26 per share'. p. 31: on 08/04 the Committee chose to continue with G&W and Party B, without mentioning E.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the 08/04 decision is read as naming the complete advancing set, E becomes Dropped by target by 08/04. Live round-3 bidders then fall from three to two between 08/04 and signing.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention (E10 requires this Question): is Party B's 08/04 revised draft merger agreement a Bid reaffirmed?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes. B returned its own mark-up after the Company moved to finalize with it; the row records a Formal $24.00 standing offer in the final round.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 31: 'On August 4, 2016, legal counsel for Party B provided a revised draft of the merger agreement'. pp. 30–31: the Company sent B a revised agreement on 08/01 and prioritized B on 08/04. On 08/12, B's price was still $1.00 below G&W's (p. 32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Without this row, B's last priced row is its round-2 LOI (#29), which is Formal but sits in a Not-final round.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention for the final-round rows: Conditions Light for B's reaffirmation and G&W's 08/12 bid; for G&W, Regulatory Concern and Antitrust blank.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Light, Regulatory Concern and Antitrust blank.
Questions.Why, with page: p. 30: the round-3 diligence was 'confirmatory'. p. 31: G&W bid with mark-ups after it 'just completed its physical diligence', and the documents were finalized that day. p. 32: the Board reviewed 'the risks associated with each process' for STB approval and found them not materially different. The filing does not describe the STB as a competition authority.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Light becomes Unclear if an express statement that only documentation remained is required. Regulatory becomes No concern if the comparative finding is read as expecting no obstacle. Antitrust becomes Y if STB review is treated as competition review.

$25.00 per common share in cash, without interest; each preferred share (with accrued unpaid dividends) is first deemed converted into 100 common shares; no CVR. Target termination fee $3,785,000 (about 3%).

DEFM14A (definitive proxy statement), dated 09/19/2016; filed 09/20/2016 per the supplied file name

None reported (Party A's Q4 2015 approach is recorded as round 0 of process 1)

Yes

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per common share, assuming conversion of the preferred stock into common (100:1); IOI and LOI ranges also given as implied equity values in $ millions

Greene Holcomb & Fisher LLC (GHF), engaged 01/27/2016; its business was acquired by BMO Capital Markets Corp. on 08/01/2016, which continued as adviser and gave the fairness opinion (fee about $2.52 million)
Hinckley, Allen & Snyder LLP; STB (regulatory) counsel, not named

In Q4 2015 Party A, a Class I rail partner, raised joint ventures and an equity investment, and PWRR's Board hired GHF (later BMO) in January 2016; on 03/14/2016 the Board chose to pursue a change-in-control process under a Transaction Committee. GHF contacted 11 strategic and 18 financial buyers in late March, 25 signed NDAs, and nine non-binding IOIs ($17.93–$26.50 per share) came in between 05/19 and 06/01/2016. The Committee dropped the two lowest bidders and gave seven access to management and a data site; late entrant Party C joined in July, six LOIs ($19.20–$24.00) arrived in late July, and two invitees did not bid. After G&W raised its CVR-bearing offer to $22.15 on price feedback, the Committee proceeded only with G&W and Party B; Parties D and E briefly re-engaged with higher but diligence-heavy offers, and D withdrew when refused a no-other-deal commitment. The Committee prioritized Party B at $24.00, but on 08/12/2016 G&W offered $25.00 in cash without the CVR; Party B would not increase, and the Board signed with G&W that day and announced the deal on 08/15/2016.
