Questions.Question: Process and round map (choice of convention). One process; round 0 = Party A's Q4 2015 approach and early board steps; round 1 opens 03/24/2016 (outreach, IOIs); round 2 at the 06/01/2016 selection of seven (LOIs); round 3 when the Committee moved to negotiate with G&W and Party B.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep this map. Round 3 is Inferred final and dated 07/27/2016 within its 07/22–07/27 window.
Questions.Why, with page: Gap ≥2 months with no acquirer contact: Party A meeting (10/01–12/31/2015) to management's 03/22/2016 Party A meeting (pp. 27–28), about 2.7–5.7 months. E5: (a) not met, GHF was hired partly for possible Party A negotiations, so Party A stayed in view; (b) possibly met; (c) met 03/14/2016. Round 3 at 07/27: G&W's $21.15 trailed Party E's $21.26 until its 07/26 revision, yet selection rested on "higher offers" (p. 30).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If round 3 opened at the 07/22 meeting, G&W's price feedback and 07/26 revision move into round 3. If round 2 opened at the mid-June LOI request, only the Round opened row moves. No supported alternative splits the process.

Questions.Question: Gap in the source: NDA population and cohort membership. The background gives 11 strategic + 14 financial March signers plus Party C (26); the reasons section says 25 (p. 33). It never says whether G&W, Parties B, D, E, F, or the two Class I railroads approached by 04/07, were among the March 11/18 contacted.
Questions.Recommended answer: Treat the 25 March signers as exact (11 + 14), with G&W, B, E, F inside the strategic cohort and D inside the financial cohort; Party C a separate entry; no entry for the two Class I railroads. Party A's Q4 2015 equity interest stays a round-0 Bidder interest of unresolved scope; Party A enters via the March NDA.
Questions.Why, with page: Every named bidder later appears as an NDA holder with the memorandum (pp. 28–29); the p. 33 total of 25 covers the six LOI bidders, consistent with named parties inside the March cohorts; the extra one (Party C) is unexplained.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If Party B, G&W or others signed outside the 25, total entries rise to 27+ and the non-IOI residual (#18) falls; if the p. 33 total is right and includes Party C, one March signer is double counted. The auction screen is Met either way.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcomes, round 1 (permitted inference). The 05/10/2016 IOI date was "subsequently postponed" to 05/19/2016, day not given; nine IOIs arrived "between May 19, 2016 and June 1, 2016" and were considered 05/23 and 06/01.
Questions.Recommended answer: 05/10: superseded before arrival (no outcome). 05/19: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: The postponement was "to ensure the potential buyers had sufficient time", implying it came before 05/10. Receipt stated as a range to 06/01 and a 06/01 review imply at least one IOI arrived after 05/19 and was considered (p. 29).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the postponement followed 05/10, that date gets a Deadline row and outcome Extended. If all IOIs came on 05/19, the outcome becomes Enforced (the Committee chose from the nine in hand).

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: which parties submitted the nine IOIs and were among the seven admitted on 06/01/2016?
Questions.Recommended answer: The seven are G&W, Parties B, D, E, F, one unnamed strategic and one unnamed financial; all were among the nine IOI bidders. Keep the non-IOI residual as "at least 16".
Questions.Why, with page: Mid-June LOIs were requested from "all potential buyers" (the seven; Party C had not yet appeared). Six LOIs came, including Party C, and "one strategic buyer and one financial buyer elected not to submit" (pp. 29–30): 5 of 7 submitted = B, G&W, D, E, F.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the LOI request reached NDA signers outside the seven, the five named bidders may not be IOI bidders, the two non-submitters may be outside the seven, and live counts at the round 2 opening change.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention on conditions: (i) IOI cohort DD Incomplete versus Party C IOI Not begun; (ii) Party E's 60-day exclusivity as Required with level Unclear; (iii) G&W's winning 08/12 bid as Regulatory Concern, Conditions Unclear.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep the coding shown.
Questions.Why, with page: (i) Cohort got "additional due diligence" after IOIs (p. 29); Party C got data-site access only after its IOI. (ii) Exclusivity is not a diligence period (E12). (iii) The Board weighed STB "risks associated with each process" for G&W and Party B (p. 32); no conditions stated for the 08/12 LOI.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Counting Party E's 60 days as a diligence period makes it Heavy (H2). Reading G&W's 08/12 LOI with mark-ups as ready to sign would make it Light; the Board's finding that approval was not materially different could support Regulatory No concern.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcome, round 2 (permitted inference). LOIs were due 07/20/2016; G&W's came 07/21 and other LOIs "in late July" without days.
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: G&W's overdue LOI was reviewed at the 07/22 and 07/27 meetings and G&W was advanced (pp. 29–30). The later price feedback and G&W's 07/26 revision are bargaining within the round.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If G&W's one-day lateness were ignored, the outcome would be Enforced (the Committee used the LOIs in hand to pick two finalists), or Passed without action if the feedback-driven revision is read as continued bidding.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: price-only revisions coded Informal: G&W 07/26/2016, Party D 08/01/2016, Party E 08/01/2016.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Informal under E11: none reports a mark-up or an express reference back to earlier Formal terms.
Questions.Why, with page: G&W's 07/21 and Party D's LOIs came with mark-ups (p. 29), but the revisions report only prices and diligence periods (pp. 29–30). The 08/03 draft to G&W reflected the mark-ups "included with G&W’s LOI" (p. 30), not a re-submission.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If revisions inherit their bidder's earlier mark-ups, G&W 07/26 and Party D 08/01 become Formal, raising the count of formal bids in rounds 2 and 3.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: Parties D and E after the 07/27 cut. They were told they were out, re-engaged on 07/29 and bid 08/01; Party E then withdrew its $23.81 revision but "confirmed its original proposal of $21.26" on 08/02 and is never mentioned again.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Re-entered for both (round 3, received but not admitted); code E's 08/02 reversion as a Bid carrying the $21.26 price and 60-day exclusivity; close E by inferred Not selected at signing.
Questions.Why, with page: E14: a returning participant within the process gets Re-entered; a reversion to an older price is a Bid (E10); "original proposal" read as incorporating its terms (p. 30); a standing offer keeps E live until signing.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the 08/02 withdrawal of the revision ended E's participation, E gets Withdrew on 08/02 and round 3 has one fewer live bidder at signing; if only the price is carried, E's 08/02 Exclusivity becomes Not stated.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: Party D's exit. Undated (after 08/01); D refused to shorten its 30-day diligence, asked for a no-sign commitment, was refused, and said it would not continue diligence "at that time".
Questions.Recommended answer: Withdrew, Exit reason Terms or process; request coded Exclusivity changed (Requested); dates bounded from 08/01 only.
Questions.Why, with page: D itself said it would not proceed (p. 30); the Company's refusal was a process term, not a rejection of D's $24.00 price.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Reading the Company's refusal as excluding D would give Dropped by target; reading D's request as a condition of continuing would code it Required. Neither changes counts.

Questions.Question: E10 Bid reaffirmed: Party B's counsel returned a revised draft merger agreement on 08/04/2016 as the Company moved to finalize with Party B.
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep a Bid reaffirmed row at $24.00, Formal, carried from Party B's LOI.
Questions.Why, with page: B's latest priced row sits in round 2, which is Not final; its own markup after the move to finalize meets E10; p. 32 shows B's price still $1.00 below G&W's $25.00 on 08/12.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Dropping the row leaves Party B's only priced bid in a non-final round, weakening the record that B held a formal $24.00 bid at the final stage.

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per common share, assuming conversion of preferred stock into common; IOIs and some bids also given as implied equity values in $ millions.
Greene Holcomb & Fisher LLC (GHF); BMO Capital Markets Corp. acquired GHF's business on 08/01/2016, continued the engagement and gave the fairness opinion.
Hinckley, Allen & Snyder LLP; unnamed STB (regulatory) counsel.

In late 2015 Party A, a Class I rail partner, floated joint ventures and an equity stake, and the Board hired GHF (later BMO) and on 03/14/2016 decided to seek a buyer. GHF contacted 11 strategic and 18 financial buyers; 25 signed confidentiality agreements and nine submitted IOIs of $17.93–$26.50 per share by 06/01/2016. Seven advanced to presentations and data-site diligence, a late strategic entrant (Party C) joined, and six LOIs arrived in late July at $19.20–$24.00, led by Party B at $24.00 while G&W raised its CVR-bearing bid to $22.15. Around 07/27 the Committee narrowed the field to Party B and G&W; Parties D and E briefly returned with higher bids, but D withdrew when refused a no-sign commitment and E reverted to $21.26. With a Party B deal set for approval on 08/12/2016, G&W, told it was losing, bid $25.00 in cash with mark-ups; Party B declined to raise, and the Board signed with G&W that day and announced on 08/15/2016.

Questions.Question: Process and round map (choice of convention): one process, with round 0 to 03/26/2013, round 1 (outreach and indications) and round 2 (final round to signing)?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes. One process. Round 1 opens 03/26/2013 (#10); round 2 opens 05/16/2013 (#38) and runs to signing. The 05/29 best-and-final request (#46) and the 06/11 demand for a single best price (#56) stay inside round 2: the round was already announced as final, and requests to improve or to name one price continue a round.
Questions.Why, with page: Gap of two months or more with no reported acquirer contact: 11/14/2012 (Company A, #2; the cancellation was communicated later, undated) to 02/13/2013 (Company B, #7), at most about three months. E5 tests: (a) met, since no offer or negotiation was outstanding; (b) not met, since the filing reports no end, the board kept reviewing (p. 24), and the gap after the undated cancellation is under three months; (c) met by the 02/13 special committee (p. 25). Outreach began six days after the 03/26 decision (p. 27); final-round letters are on p. 30.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative boundary: process 1 = #1–#5 (the November 2012 review and Company A) lapses, and process 2 restarts at #6 with an inferred Process restarted row; no bidder periods need closing. Alternative rounds: round 1 opens at 04/01 (outreach) or 04/23 (letters); round 3 opens at #46 or #56, moving WDC’s 06/10 and 06/14 bids into round 3.

Questions.Question: Scope of Companies C, E and F and of the asset-only interests (choice of convention). The board weighed asset sales against a whole-company sale (#11), and six strategic parties expressed asset-only interest. Who is in the whole-company contest?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep Company C partial-only from its first approach (#8, #18): no entry, no exit. Treat Companies E and F as whole-company entrants through their sale NDAs (#15, #17) that withdrew by switching to asset-only interest (#23, #24). Keep the other asset-only parties inside the contact cohort (#13), with no rows of their own.
Questions.Why, with page: Company C first expressed interest in “particular assets” (p. 26). E and F signed NDAs “related to the exploration of a potential sale of the company” (p. 28); their asset-only statements came later (p. 28). The filing does not say whether C, E, F or G are among the 18 parties or the six asset-only parties (p. 27).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If E and F were partial from the start: no entries or exits for them, whole-company NDA signers fall from 6 to 4 (auction screen still Met), and round 1 has 4 entrants. If Company C is one of the 18, the residual cohort in #13 is 13.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcome for the round-1 due date of 05/03/2013 (choice of convention).
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted).
Questions.Why, with page: WDC answered on time and Company G withdrew (p. 29). Company D asked on 05/02 for another week (p. 29); no new date is reported. Its 05/10 written indication was received, and on 05/15 it was allowed to continue (p. 29). Company H signed its NDA on 05/08 and was not eligible.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If Company D’s request is read as granted with a new date, the outcome is Extended and #27 becomes a Deadline revised row. Bids, exits and round membership do not change.

Questions.Question: Deadline outcomes for round 2: 05/28/2013 and 05/30/2013 (choice of convention).
Questions.Recommended answer: 05/28: Extended (on 05/29 the board set a best-and-final date of 05/30). 05/30: Enforced (that day the board moved forward with WDC on the bids in hand).
Questions.Why, with page: Final-round letters were due 05/28 (p. 30). On 05/29 the board asked for best-and-final proposals by 05/30 (pp. 30–31). Company D missed both dates but continued (#44, #48). On 05/31 it was invited to continue, with no due date (#51, p. 31); it withdrew 06/05 (p. 32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternatives: 05/30 is Passed without action if keeping Company D in play after WDC’s pull-back counts as continued bidding; #46 is a Deadline set (a new solicitation) rather than a revision. Only labels change.

Questions.Question: Company H’s status after the round-1 price feedback (permitted inference).
Questions.Recommended answer: No exit at the feedback (#40): Company H was told its range could not advance but that it could submit a revised indication, so it stayed in reserve. Close it with an inferred Not selected at signing (#65). Exit reason: Would not improve earlier offer, because it was invited to improve and declined (#41).
Questions.Why, with page: Feedback and invitation to revise: p. 30. Company H stayed interested but could not raise its range (05/23, p. 30). At signing the board weighed Company H’s ability to make a superior proposal and noted it had “repeatedly” refused to go above $5.00–$5.75 (pp. 34–35).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative: Dropped by target at #40 (refused the next stage), Exit reason Lower offer than rivals. Live units at the round-2 opening would then be 2, not 3, and Company H would leave Rounds’ “still being received” list. Or keep #65 with Exit reason Not stated.

Questions.Question: Formality and Conditions of WDC’s bids #43, #55 and #57 (choice of convention).
Questions.Recommended answer: #43 Formal (merger agreement markup, answering the final-round letter). #55 and #57 Formal by WDC’s express reference to its 05/28 terms. Conditions Unclear on all three: diligence was open and no condition was stated. Financing is Not stated at the bid dates, although the signed agreement has no financing condition (p. 36).
Questions.Why, with page: Markup and ancillary drafts: p. 30. “Otherwise prepared to move forward on the transaction terms previously proposed on May 28”: p. 32. Diligence stopped 05/31 (p. 31) and resumed 06/16–06/22, “including confirmatory” calls (p. 33).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Heavy (H3) on #43 if WDC’s demand for the founders’ covenant not to sue and other ancillary agreements is read as a prerequisite that proceeding depended on. #55 is Informal if a range “indication of interest” does not carry the Formal markup. #57 is Light if the June diligence counts as only confirmatory.

Questions.Question: Is WDC’s pull-back on 05/31/2013 an exit (permitted inference; choice of convention)?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes. Withdrew (Other stated reason) on 05/31 (#50), and Re-entered on 06/10 (#54) before its revised bid.
Questions.Why, with page: WDC said it was “not prepared to move forward with a transaction with sTec at that time” and stopped due diligence (p. 31). E14 counts “for now” withdrawals. It returned with a lower bid on 06/10 (p. 32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If WDC’s participation is treated as continuing (the 06/01–06/10 talks), drop both rows. Live whole-company units from 05/31 to 06/10 would rise by one; between 06/05 and 06/10 Company H would otherwise be the only live unit.

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per share; all priced bids in cash except Company D’s verbal floor (consideration not stated)
BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated)

Facing losses and an activist campaign, sTec’s board began a review of strategic alternatives, including a sale, in November 2012 and formed a special committee in February 2013. After unsolicited approaches from Companies A, B, C and D, BofA Merrill Lynch contacted 18 prospective acquirers from April 2013. Six signed NDAs, and WDC, Company D and Company H submitted indications of interest; Companies E, F and C wanted only assets. WDC bid $9.15 in the final round, which the board accepted on 05/30, but WDC pulled back the next day, Company D disengaged, and WDC returned with a range of $6.60–$7.10. Pressed for a single best offer, WDC bid $6.85 as its best and final price, and the parties signed on 06/23/2013 and announced on 06/24/2013.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention / source gap: Is this one continuing process with two organized rounds, despite the early contact gap and WDC’s temporary withdrawal?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep one process: preliminary round 0, round 1 at March 26 authorization implemented April 1, and final round 2 at May 16 letters. May 29 best-and-final request and June return continue round 2. Alternative: separate February 13 fresh start if the early hiatus qualifies; move #7 onward to process 2.
Questions.Why, with page: Only approximately two-month-plus gap in dated sale narrative: last A follow-up/cancellation in 11/14–11/29/2012 to B contact 02/13/2013 (76–91 days). E5(a): no carry-forward not established; review continued and A is later contacted. (b): no reported termination; undated endpoint straddles roughly-three-month threshold, so do not round up. (c): yes, February 13 committee mandate. Not all tests pass. May 31–June 10: (a) fails, D continues; (b) fails, ongoing contacts/short interval; (c) renewed discussions, no distinct fresh mandate/outreach. Earlier 2011 and summer-2012 lunches lack month-level dating and remain Deal facts (pp. 24–32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative early split gives two processes, first with no organized round/NDA and second with these two rounds. Another plausible round boundary is May 10 data-room access; it would move #42–#49 to round 2, but no common final selection is yet established. Deal facts.Value: US dollars per sTec common share. Cash only where stated; D’s Apr 23 oral proposal leaves mix Not stated. Strict “greater than $5.60” lower bound retained. No CVR/earnout reported. Dollar definition: Annex A §1.3(g), p. A-7.

Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP, outside corporate counsel engaged October 2012 (p. 25). Latham & Watkins LLP, litigation counsel to sTec and Manouch Moshayedi, first dated participation in weeks of May 13/20 (p. 29). Paul Hastings represents the Moshayedis, not sTec (p. 33).

sTec began reviewing strategic alternatives in late 2012 amid losses, while Balch Hill and later Potomac pressed for changes. An independent committee selected BofA Merrill Lynch and launched a primarily strategic-buyer outreach in spring 2013. The banker discussed transactions with 18 parties, and WDC, Company D and Company H submitted whole-company indications. WDC and D received final-round letters, but D repeatedly needed more time, while H could not raise its range and was not advanced. WDC offered $9.15, withdrew, then returned with a lower range after internal disagreement, and D disengaged. sTec accepted WDC’s $6.85 cash offer, signed June 23, 2013 and announced June 24; no later competing proposal or go-shop is reported.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: one process and two rounds, or an earlier restart/advancement boundary?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep one process. Round 1 opens March 26 authorization executed April 1; round 2 opens May 16 final solicitation. Earlier data-room access is diligence within round 1. May 31 continues the final stage.
Questions.Why, with page: Gap: last A contact/cancellation 11/14–11/29/2012 to B contact 02/13/2013 (76–91 days). E5(a): met—no offer/negotiation carried; (b): not established—undated endpoint, no reported termination; (c): met—February 13 committee. Earlier 2011-to-summer-2012 and summer-2012-to-November-14 contacts lack month precision and remain Earlier approaches (pp. 24–27). No later two-month pre-signing contact gap.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative: a February 13 restart if the gap satisfies E5(b), moving that row onward to process 2; or open round 2 May 10–15 at access/conditional advancement, moving those rows and some initial offers. Recommended explicit final solicitation avoids treating access alone as selection.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: did D’s May 2 request establish a May 10 extended deadline? Was H late?
Questions.Recommended answer: May 3: Extended (late bid accepted). No dated extension was granted expressly, so no May 10 Deadline or Deadline revised row. H was not solicited by May 3; its May 15 offer is not late.
Questions.Why, with page: WDC/D invited April 23, G April 26 (p. 28). D requested another week May 2 and submitted May 10; H contacted May 1, signed May 8, presented May 10 and bid May 15 (p. 29).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If inferred grant is preferred, add inferred May 2 Deadline revised and May 10 Deadline; recode May 3 Extended. Do not infer H’s eligibility from its later NDA.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how did the May 28 and May 30 final-round deadlines operate?
Questions.Recommended answer: May 28 Extended to May 30; May 30 Enforced when target selected WDC. D missed both but remained available, then withdrew June 5. No extra round or premature exit.
Questions.Why, with page: Final letter May 16; D sought two weeks May 28; both solicited for May 30 on May 29 (p. 30). Board chose WDC May 30 and invited D to continue May 31 (p. 31). No later due date or overdue final D offer.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative May 30 Passed without action if continued availability outweighs board selection; participation and June 5 exit stay unchanged.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: how do early approaches and anonymous contacts reconcile to the 18-party outreach?
Questions.Recommended answer: Preserve 18 = 17 strategic + 1 financial. A, D and H explicitly belong; residual contact row is 14 strategic. Do not add their earlier contacts again. C may overlap; B and earlier financial contacts have unproven overlap.
Questions.Why, with page: Outreach total and partitions: three whole-company bidders, six asset-interest parties, nine uninterested (p. 27). Six NDA parties are E/D/F/G/WDC/H (pp. 27–29). E/F counted in six asset-interest parties; C is plausible, not expressly established as a banker contact.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Unnamed asset residual stays 3–4; no inferred exits for mere contacts. Resolving C/B membership changes anonymous identities and unique-contact totals, not the six NDA entries or three priced bidders.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: were E and F partial-only from entry? Are asset-interest statements bids?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep E/F NDA entries until their dated switches to assets; E1 forbids back-projecting later scope. C is partial-only from first contact. Record interest and termination, not Other-scope bid, because no communicated asset proposal is reported.
Questions.Why, with page: E/F sign April 4/11 (p. 27), clarify asset-only scope April 24/shortly afterward (p. 28). Page 34 later describes solely asset interest without dating it to entry. C contemplated submitting a proposal March 13 but only asset interest is later reported (pp. 26, 28).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative excludes E/F throughout: remove their whole-company exits; NDA auction screen still Met with WDC/D/G/H (four). If interest alone is treated as a proposal, add Other-scope bids, never whole-company bids.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: how should price precision, formality and unstated bid conditions be coded?
Questions.Recommended answer: D’s April 23 proposal is strictly above $5.60; retain open-bound qualifier. May 28 WDC Formal via markup/final solicitation; June 10/14 Formal through express May 28 incorporation. Other first-round bids Informal. Keep unspecified condition levels Unclear.
Questions.Why, with page: D’s verbal proposal and additional diligence p. 28; initial written offers p. 29; May 28 markup p. 30; later incorporation p. 32. Signing-only cash/funding representation p. 36 and A-23 does not establish earlier financing. May 30 unchanged Formal offer earns no reaffirmation row.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Treating April 23 as valuation removes one D bid, not entry. Rejecting express incorporation would change June bids’ formality; no later funding/diligence evidence should be moved backward.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: when did Company H’s participation end?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep H in reserve, outside final-stage admission, until inferred Not selected at signing June 23. Exit reason Would not improve earlier offer; no re-entry needed.
Questions.Why, with page: H invited to improve despite denial of advancement; May 23 expressly remained interested but could not increase range (p. 30). Board considered H’s ability to top WDC at signing (pp. 34–35).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative exit on refusal May 23 lowers late-round live competition by one; it conflicts with express continued interest and signing-date consideration.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: did WDC withdraw on May 31 or merely pause?
Questions.Recommended answer: Record Withdrew May 31 (“at that time”), then Re-entered June 10 with its revised offer. June 1–10 strategy discussions do not establish an earlier return to active participation.
Questions.Why, with page: WDC said not prepared to proceed and stopped diligence (p. 31). It reconsidered internally and returned with $6.60–$7.10 cash plus May 28 terms June 10 (p. 32). D continued; no E5 process break.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Treating this as a pause removes withdrawal/re-entry and adds WDC to the live count during the interval. Offer prices and two-round map remain unchanged.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: does WDC’s threat over NDA waivers materially revise its commitment?
Questions.Recommended answer: Yes: retain an unpriced Formal Bid, Heavy under H3, for June 20–23. Proceeding explicitly depended on retaining “don’t ask, don’t waive” provisions. Do not carry price/mix absent express incorporation in this communication.
Questions.Why, with page: June 20 revised agreement and refusal to negotiate further (p. 33); threatened not to proceed if target waived provisions, followed by target acceptance (pp. 34–35). Diligence ran June 16–22 (p. 33).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative treats this as legal bargaining and uses Other material event instead; removes a commitment-revision bid but leaves price series and competition restriction recorded.

mixed — board-led strategic review, unsolicited approaches and activist pressure (pp. 24–27).

Deal facts.Field: Currency and units of bid prices
Deal facts.Value: US dollars per common share. D’s first oral offer strictly greater than $5.60; open-bound qualifier retained. All stated written offer mixes cash.
BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated); selected 03/26/2013, engagement signed 03/28/2013 (p. 27).
Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP: outside corporate counsel since October 2012 (p. 25). Latham & Watkins LLP: litigation counsel to sTec and Manouch Moshayedi, acting in May diligence (p. 29).

sTec explored a sale as losses and strategic difficulties persisted, while Balch Hill and Potomac pressed for changes. BofA Merrill Lynch contacted 18 potential acquirers, and six strategic parties signed sale-related confidentiality instruments. WDC, Company D and Company H proposed whole-company purchases; other interest concerned selected assets. WDC and D entered the final solicitation, while H remained interested but unable to improve its lower range. WDC offered $9.15 cash, withdrew, and returned at $6.60–$7.10 before fixing its price at $6.85; D ultimately disengaged. sTec signed with WDC on June 23 and announced the agreement June 24, with no go-shop or later competing offer reported.

BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated), approved 03/26/2013, engagement letter 03/28/2013

Facing losses and an activist campaign by Balch Hill and Potomac, sTec's board began a strategic review in late 2012 and formed a special committee on 02/13/2013, while Companies A, B, C and D made early approaches. After hiring BofA Merrill Lynch, sTec had discussions with 18 prospective acquirers from 04/01/2013; six signed NDAs, several wanted only selected assets, and WDC ($6.60–7.10), Company D ($5.75) and late entrant Company H ($5.00–5.75) made whole-company indications. WDC and D received final-round letters with a draft merger agreement; WDC bid $9.15 with a markup and confirmed it as best, while D kept asking for more time. The board chose WDC on 05/30, but WDC withdrew the next day and D disengaged on 06/05 despite an invitation to continue. WDC returned on 06/10 with a $6.60–7.10 range, was told to name a single best offer, bid $6.85 on 06/14 and refused further negotiation or standstill waivers. The board accepted without countering, signed the $6.85 cash merger on 06/23/2013 and announced it on 06/24/2013.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: where does the process and its rounds begin, and does WDC’s June return open another process or round?
Questions.Recommended answer: One process. The sale review began mid-November 2012; round 1 opened March 26, 2013; round 2 opened May 16. WDC returned within round 2.
Questions.Why, with page: The board continued its strategic review after two advisers declined (p. 24). E5(a): no earlier party was shown carrying forward after Company A’s cancelled meeting; (b): no termination was reported and Company A’s last contact/cancellation is undated, so a full three-month break cannot be proved; (c): the February committee and March outreach are fresh steps (pp. 25–27). The interval from Company A’s November 14 contact to Company B’s February 13 contact is about three months, with an undated Company A cancellation inside it. No other two-month acquirer-contact gap occurs in the mapped process. WDC and the banker remained in discussion June 1–10 (pp. 31–32).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: Alternative: treat February 13 as process 2 if the undated Company A cancellation occurred in November and review continuity is discounted; move all February–June rows to process 2 and close process 1. Alternative round boundary: April 1 outreach rather than March 26 decision moves the March 26 marker to April 1. Another possible boundary is June 10, but there was no new target solicitation.

Questions.Question: Decision for researchers: what happened to the May 3 first-round due date when Company D delivered May 10?
Questions.Recommended answer: Extended (late bid accepted). D requested about a week on May 2; no new due date set by sTec is reported. WDC responded on time, G withdrew, and D’s late written offer was considered.
Questions.Why, with page: Process letters requested May 3 from WDC and D (p. 28), then G (p. 28); D asked for more time May 2, WDC bid/G exited May 3, and D bid May 10 (p. 29). The May 15 continuation confirms acceptance (p. 29).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the May 2 request was an accepted new May 10 date, call the first due date Extended and add the later operative due date and outcome; the filing never reports that acceptance.

Questions.Question: Decision for researchers: how should the May 28 and May 30 final-round deadlines be coded?
Questions.Recommended answer: May 28: Extended because the board set a May 30 best-and-final due date for both bidders on May 29. May 30: Enforced because the board chose WDC that day; D missed but continued as reserve until June 5.
Questions.Why, with page: Final letters sought May 28 (p. 30). D asked for approximately two more weeks May 28; the board instead requested May 30 responses May 29; WDC held price, D sought time, and board selected WDC May 30 (pp. 30–31). D was invited back May 31 (p. 31).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: A soft deadline reading would make May 30 Passed without action, but the same-day board selection supports Enforced. Treating D as dropped May 30 would require a re-entry on May 31 and would overstate closure.

Questions.Question: Gap in source: which of Companies C, E and F, and the six partial-interest prospects, ever sought the whole company?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep C outside the contest; E and F outside whole-company counts because they later stated they were only interested in selected assets. Treat the six partial interests as a reported cohort whose membership is uncertain, not six additional distinct parties. Auction screen remains Met through WDC, D, G and H.
Questions.Why, with page: C considered only particular assets (p. 26); E and F signed NDAs but later said they only wanted selected assets (pp. 27–28). The 18 prospects split 3 whole-company bidders, 6 partial interests and 9 uninterested, without naming every member (p. 27). Six NDAs are named (p. 28).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If E/F were seeking a whole-company sale under NDA before a scope switch, add each as a live bidder on its NDA date and an exit at the later partial-interest statement; round 1 live count and auction-screen count rise. Do not add their partial interest to whole-company bids.

Questions.Question: Choice of convention: do WDC’s June revisions retain Formal status, and can Company D’s April verbal lower bound be entered?
Questions.Recommended answer: Code WDC June 10 and June 14 Formal because each expressly carries May 28 terms, which included merger markup. Enter D’s strict lower bound as Price low 5.60, with “greater than” in its Note. Leave bid-date financing as Not stated.
Questions.Why, with page: WDC submitted markup May 28 (p. 30); June 10 and June 14 said prior transaction terms remained (p. 32). D’s April 23 verbal indication was greater than $5.60 (p. 28). WDC financing representation appears only at agreement signing (p. 36; Annex A), with no express earlier date.
Questions.What changes if answered differently: If the June references are read as excluding definitive markup, recode June bids Informal. If a strict greater-than threshold is judged unsuitable for a numeric low cell, clear D’s Price low while retaining the quoted threshold in its Note.

Questions.Question: Permitted inference: did Company H leave on May 15 or May 23, or remain a continuing alternative until signing?
Questions.Recommended answer: Keep H live but not admitted to the final round, then infer Not selected at signing. Its revision was expressly allowed, it reaffirmed interest May 23, and the board considered H’s superior-proposal potential June 23.
Questions.Why, with page: H’s range was insufficient for advancement, but a revision would be considered (p. 30). H remained interested at same range May 23 (p. 30). Board considered H under its NDA standstill at signing (pp. 34–35).
Questions.What changes if answered differently: An alternative marks H Dropped by target when told its range was insufficient; this decreases live rivals earlier, but then its May 23 continuing interest and June 23 board review require reserve status and should not be treated as a fresh bid.

sTec began reviewing strategic alternatives in late 2012 while facing losses and activist pressure. A special committee was appointed in February 2013, and the board directed confidential outreach to likely strategic buyers in March. BofA spoke with 18 prospects; WDC, Company D and Company H made whole-company indications, while other prospects either wanted assets or declined. Final-round letters went to WDC and D in May, and WDC offered $9.15 before withdrawing on May 31. D disengaged June 5; WDC returned with a lower range and then $6.85 cash, which sTec accepted and signed on June 23. The merger was announced June 24.
